purpose: Independent expected failure vectors for tools/check-section-citations.py (round-16 C1 claim: correct two section citations routed in corpus/lessons/round-15-verifier-spotcheck.md). Static fixture; nothing here was executed. Finding ids and exit codes mirror the check-locator-clarification.py convention: PASS=0, FAIL=1, CANNOT_EVALUATE=2; ids named R16-* plus the actual-defect detector SECTION-CITATION-WRONG and the E-* cannot-evaluate family.

gate.selftest: --selftest (hermetic in-memory fixtures, fixed expected exit + finding ids)
gate.count_semantics: correction_count = number of the two records that are individually valid and not blocked by any common/shared finding; shared findings (schema, count, id, history, supersession, source-row, opener/heading/md-scope) block both records; record-scoped findings block only their own record; SECTION-CITATION-WRONG at a target site blocks only the record owning that file
gate.resolution_semantics: For each record: heading must equal the contract string exactly and exist as a Markdown heading line in record.path; row_key must equal the contract value and match exactly one row line under that heading; quote must be a substring of that resolved row; notice_heading must equal the contract value, exist appended to record.path, and link the correction id, the quoted old_locator, a 'supersedes the citation only' scope sentence, the preserved R15-UPDATE-STATE reference, and a no-package/service-authorization sentence. The historical wrong locator literal is tolerated only inside the preserved R15-UPDATE-STATE section or quoted inside its resolving R16 notice; any other occurrence yields SECTION-CITATION-WRONG.
gate.history_semantics: For each target file, bytes up to the start of its appended '## R16-*-SECTION — citation-only erratum' section must equal the baseline prefix (digest-pinned, e.g. sha256 of baseline file content for both targets since no bytes were added before the notice); any earlier-byte change yields R16-HISTORY-REWRITTEN (count 0). The '## R15-UPDATE-STATE (2026-10-20) — current-use supersession' section must remain present and unrouted-away; removing or re-superseding it yields R16-SUPERSESSION-REMOVED.

gate.fixture_note: clean fixture = baseline file bytes with the delivered R16 notices appended (verbatim as committed) plus the delivered errata pair and S050 row; baseline fixture = baseline bytes with md16/json16 absent and no R16 notice sections.
gate.false_positive_guard: Legitimate §7 mentions in v3 ('v2 §7's table' line 210, 'v2's §7 ranks' line 366) and §1 mentions in r3 ('R3-1 §1.1' line 262, 'Gap vs §1's' line 425, '§0.1's index' line 442) are NOT defects; the detector binds only to the literal wrong locators '§1 verdict-board row 5' / '§7 rank 1' (whitespace-normalized) outside preserved notice context. r3 really contains a '## 1.' heading and v3 a '## 7.' heading, so heading resolution must not be satisfied by section-number coincidence.

finding_vocabulary.defect: SECTION-CITATION-WRONG (site = the target file containing the wrong-locator text)

cases.assertion: Positive case: valid pair plus appended notices passes.

cases.mutation: all four files at baseline bytes; md16/json16 absent; --revision db68e62065885b3f7463eb0a436c41f0dc3bcde5 gives the same result
cases.assertion: Baseline actual bad locators are detected: r3 line 581 '§1 verdict-board row 5' (true §0) and v3 line 398 '§7 rank 1' (true §5); detail strings must contain the literal wrong locator.
Notices alone do not resolve: with no valid correction record linking id/old_locator/notice_heading, the preserved wrong locators remain unresolvable defects.
Companion entry file absence fails the run without invalidating the JSON records.
Unparseable corrections file is cannot-evaluate, not a conformance failure.
Sibling schema string is rejected; only tsukuroi-section-citation-errata-v1 counts.
The orphaned v3 notice cannot resolve without its record, so the §7 rank 1 defect re-opens.
Without the declared old_locator the gate cannot bind the notice to the defect; rank record still counts.
Record must point at the file its defect lives in; resolution then fails and the r3 defect re-opens.
